newsitem.title: USA: NYC FY '97 tax revenues $289 mln above plan - report.
newsitem.headline: NYC FY '97 tax revenues $289 mln above plan - report.

text.p: New York City's fiscal year 1997 tax revenues are $289 million above plan, city Comptroller Alan Hevesi said in a his budget notes report Monday.
For the first three months of fiscal year 1997, which began July 1, total cumulative tax revenues including audits were $289 million above plan, the comptroller's report said.
"This is good news for the city," the comptroller's report said. "The extra revenue should provide some of the funds needed to close the gap in FY 97 budget."

The report also notes that if the "current trend continues, the city could end the year $500 million more in tax revenues than projected in the financial plan. However, it is too early to count on rising revenues to solve the city's fiscal problems."
The bulk of the revenues came from the general property and the general corporation tax, which were $159 million and $85 million, respectively, over the financial plan, the report said.
The property tax revenue increase resulted in part from the early payment of second quarter taxes to gain a two percent prepayment discount, the report stated.

"The increase in the general corporation tax of $85 million came in part from higher quarterly estimated payments, which means that some companies, in particular securities firms, are expecting higher profits," the report said. "If there were to be a reversal in the performance of the financial market, the impact on the general corporation tax could be negative."
Most of the FY 1997 first quarter tax revenue increase in came in September, which was $216 million above plan.
The report said some of the revenue increases resulted from technical factors and may not indicate a trend.

Also, the potential effect a weakening city economy in the first quarter of FY 1997 -- as suggested by the decline in employment in July and August -- has not indicated what direction the city economy will take for the remainder of the fiscal year, the report said.
